```plato
//==
// # Implicit shape interfaces
//
// Shapes described by functions rather than boundaries. A signed distance
// field (SDF; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signed_distance_function) reports
// how far a point is from a surface, negative inside; an implicit region
// reports only membership (see also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implicit_surface).
// The concrete types implementing these interfaces are declared in
// `implicit-sdf.types.plato`.
//
// Distance fidelity — what a returned value MEANS. There are three cases, and
// which one a field returns decides whether a sphere tracer is correct:
//
//  - EXACT: the value is the true signed distance, so the gradient has unit
//    length almost everywhere (the eikonal property). Marching takes maximal
//    steps, `Offset` gives the true offset surface, and the unit gradient is
//    the true surface normal.
//  - LOWER BOUND: the value never exceeds the true distance. Marching still
//    converges, in shorter steps; offsets and normals are wrong, but no
//    surface is stepped over.
//  - NOT A BOUND: the value may EXCEED the true distance, so a sphere tracer
//    stepping by it steps past the surface and tunnels through it. That is a
//    correctness failure, not a quality one. A field that is k-Lipschitz for a
//    known k greater than one is a lower bound again once divided by k.
//
// Fidelity is a property of a VALUE's construction history, not of a type — one
// `FunctionSdf3D` holds an exact sphere and another holds a twisted
// approximation of one — so no interface here records it. Every primitive and
// operator in `implicit-sdf.library.plato` and `fields-implicits.library.plato`
// says which of the three it returns, in those words, and `EikonalResidualAt`
// measures the departure from exact where the claim is not trusted. Those claims
// describe the EXTERIOR, where marching runs; inside a Min or Max combination
// the value is the depth below the nearest operand surface, which is shallower
// than the depth below the combined one.
//
// Unbounded vs bounded: `ISignedDistanceField2D/3D` are pure distance oracles
// with no finite domain. `IBoundedSignedDistanceField2D/3D` add a conservative
// AABB (`IBounded2D/3D`) for culling and acceleration; `DistanceAt` /
// `Eval` still evaluate the underlying field everywhere — bounds are hints,
// not a change to distance semantics. Analytic wrappers live in
// `implicit-sdf.types.plato`; sampled lattices (`SampledSdf*`) already
// carry a `Bounds` spanning their finite support and implement the bounded
// interfaces.
//
// Differentiable: `IDifferentiableSignedDistanceField2D/3D` add a gradient, which
// for a distance field is the outward normal direction. They inherit
// `IDifferentiableScalarField2D/3D` (`fields.concepts.plato`), so every helper
// derived from a gradient there — `SurfaceNormalAt`, `BoundaryNormalAt`,
// `SlopeAt` — resolves against an SDF that reports one. Reporting a gradient is
// a separate claim from reporting a distance: a field whose values are only a
// lower bound still has a gradient, but it is not the surface normal.

// A planar scalar field whose value is the signed distance to a boundary
// curve: negative inside, zero on the boundary, positive outside. The value may
// be exact, a lower bound, or not a bound at all; which one is stated per
// operation and never carried by the type (fidelity, above).
interface ISignedDistanceField2D
    inherits IScalarField2D
{ }
```
